cohort: Pregnant women who underwent an invasive procedure during one of their pregnancies (n=61) compared to pregnant women who did not undergo an invasive procedure (n=122)
finding: Non-obstetric invasive procedures during pregnancy are associated with an increased rate of cesarean sections and lower birth weight, but no significant differences in early perinatal outcome were found.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was significantly higher in women who underwent a non-obstetric invasive procedure during pregnancy.
birth_weight: Birth weight range was approximately 2908g to 3185g
